We need answer JSON only. Need evaluate every story PP-001 to PP-053 for Conceptually sound criterion. Need understand criterion: Means expresses a feature and ends expresses a rationale for that feature. Violation when means does not state a feature, or when ends introduces another required feature instead of explaining why means is valuable. Scope individual. Need classify each story.

We need be careful. User story format "As a role, I want <means>, so that <ends>". Need assess means states feature? ends rationale? violation if means not feature or ends introduces another required feature instead of explaining why means valuable.

Need evaluate all 53. We can produce JSON. Need concise evidence/rationale. Related story ids: likely empty for individual. But if set-level? criterion individual, no related required. We can include empty list.

Need avoid uncertain. For each story decide violation/no.

Let's parse each. Need possible violations. We need classify exactly. Let's go through.

PP-001: As moderator, I want to create a new game by entering a name and optional description, so that I can start inviting estimators.
Means: create a new game by entering name/desc — feature. Ends: start inviting estimators — rationale? It explains why create game valuable (enables next step). Not another required feature? "start inviting estimators" could be seen another feature (invite estimators) from PP-002? But criterion says ends introduces another required feature instead of explaining why means is valuable. Here ends "so that I can start inviting estimators" maybe introduces another required feature "inviting estimators" rather than rationale? Need determine. The means create game; ends to start inviting estimators is an outcome/rationale, not the same feature. It may be legitimate. Many user stories naturally have ends as next activity. But QUS "Conceptually sound" from Lucassen: means feature, ends rationale. Example violation if means doesn't state feature or ends introduces another required feature instead of explaining why means valuable. We need apply strict? "so that I can start inviting estimators" is why create game is valuable? It is a capability. Hmm.

Let's recall Lucassen QUS criteria. Conceptually sound: The means expresses a feature and the ends expresses a rationale for that feature. A user story is conceptually sound if it is not a "feature decomposition" (ends is another feature) and not "why" missing. Could be violation if "so that" is another user story. In many backlogs, PP-001 ends "start inviting estimators" references PP-002. But that doesn't necessarily mean violation? It might be introducing another required feature. Criterion says violation when ends introduces another required feature instead of explaining why the means is valuable. "I can start inviting estimators" is a rationale, value. Hmm.

We need evaluate using criterion, not from ideal. Could classify PP-001 no violation likely.

Let's inspect all.

PP-002: As moderator, I want to invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game, so that we can start the game.
Means invite estimators via URL—feature. Ends: we can start game—rationale? This may be another feature? "start the game" maybe an activity. It explains why invite. Acceptable probably.

PP-003: create round by entering item, so that we can estimate it. Means feature, ends rationale "we can estimate it" (value). No violation.

PP-004: see all items we try to estimate this session, so that I can answer questions about current story such as "does this include ___". Means feature, ends rationale. No violation.

PP-005: select item to be estimated/re-estimated, so team sees item and can estimate it. Means feature, ends rationale. No violation.

PP-006: As moderator, I want to add an item to the list of items to be estimated, so that so that we can be flexible and accommodate situations where we think of a new story while playing. There's typo "so that so that". Means feature add item. Ends rationale flexibility. No violation. Typo not criterion.

PP-007: edit item, so that I can make it better reflect team's understanding. No violation.

PP-008: delete item, so that we can remove it and not estimate it. Means delete feature. Ends "remove it and not estimate it" is almost restating means? Does it express rationale? It explains why delete: to remove and not estimate. Could be tautological but still rationale. Not violation under criterion? It might be too trivial, but not "introduces another required feature". No violation.

PP-009: As moderator, I want to show all estimates immediately, so that I can decide to show the estimates that have been given even though not all estimators have given their estimate.
Means: show all estimates immediately. Ends: "I can decide to show estimates that have been given even though not all estimators have given" This appears restates means? Wait "show all estimates immediately" means all including perhaps not all? The end says decide to show estimates that have been given even though not all... It's more of same feature, maybe rationale? It explains why immediate show. Could be semantically awkward: "I want to show all estimates immediately, so that I can decide to show the estimates..." The end is essentially the feature, not a rationale. Does it introduce another required feature? It says decide to show estimates—maybe same feature. Criterion requires ends rationale.
